# Beyond Screens and Video Internship — 180-Day Program

**Duration:** 180 days · 8 hours per day · 1,440 guided hours

Prepare interns to perform screens and video work safely, ethically, measurably, reproducibly, and professionally under Beyond supervision.

## Program-wide safety and professional rules

- Use approved lifts, stands, rigging, PPE, and spotters. Calculate power, secure equipment and cables, establish exclusion zones, and follow approved power-down rules before connector or module work.
- Work only inside authorized boundaries and on assigned assets.
- Capture evidence during work; preserve prior evidence and restore the approved state.
- Use official/vendor sources, approved tools, rated hardware, valid licences, and qualified supervision.
- Protect secrets, personal/client data, recordings, equipment details, and production information.
- Document measurements, uncertainty, errors, troubleshooting, time, assistance, incidents, and limitations honestly.

## Program phases

- **Electrical, Lifting, and Screen Safety** — Days 1-10
- **Video Fundamentals** — Days 11-20
- **Connectors, Cables, and Signal Transport** — Days 21-30
- **LED Screen Components and Assembly** — Days 31-40
- **LED Processing and Configuration** — Days 41-50
- **Projection Systems** — Days 51-60
- **Video Switching and Routing** — Days 61-70
- **Cameras and Image Acquisition** — Days 71-80
- **Media Playback and Graphics** — Days 81-90
- **Streaming and Recording** — Days 91-100
- **Color Calibration and Quality Control** — Days 101-110
- **Signal Distribution and Redundancy** — Days 111-120
- **Video over IP and Networked Media** — Days 121-130
- **Large-Format Design and Pixel Mapping** — Days 131-140
- **Event and Broadcast Workflows** — Days 141-150
- **Troubleshooting and Maintenance** — Days 151-160
- **Site Planning, Rigging, and Production Management** — Days 161-170
- **Screens and Video Capstone and Career Readiness** — Days 171-180

---

# STUDY NOTES — Day 1: Orientation and setup: Electrical, Lifting, and Screen Safety

Beyond Screens and Video internship notes prepare students to apply **Electrical, Lifting, and Screen Safety** safely, ethically, measurably, and professionally under human supervision.

## 1. DAY FOCUS

**Mode:** Orientation and setup  
**Topic:** Electrical, Lifting, and Screen Safety  
**Phase:** Electrical, Lifting, and Screen Safety  
**Difficulty:** foundation · **Estimated time:** 8h  
**Tools for this day:** Beyond LED screens, projectors, PPE, approved lifts/stands, distribution tools, checklists

**Objective:** Complete a supervised electrical, lifting, stand/rigging, cable-trip, power-down, and exclusion-zone readiness check before installing or energizing screens and video equipment.

## 2. LEARNING OUTCOMES

- Explain Electrical, Lifting, and Screen Safety in clear professional language.
- Use Beyond LED screens, projectors, PPE to complete the objective inside the approved boundary.
- Produce measurable, independently verified evidence for: Complete a supervised electrical, lifting, stand/rigging, cable-trip, power-down, and exclusion-zone readiness check before installing or energizing screens and video equipment.
- Apply Beyond safety, ethics, quality, documentation, rollback, and human-approval standards.

## 3. CORE CONCEPTS

**Topic focus:** Electrical, Lifting, and Screen Safety. Define meaningful professional concepts rather than splitting the title into isolated words. Connect every concept to an observable action, measurement/control, evidence item, and failure mode.

**Key terms and ideas to define in the report:**

- Electrical, Lifting, and Screen Safety
- PPE exclusion zones and supervised lifting
- power load grounding and distribution
- stands frames rated hardware and secondary safety
- cable ramps trip control and emergency power-down

## 4. PRACTICAL PROCEDURE

**Prerequisite:** Program admission, assigned authorized workstation/equipment, and approved lab or venue boundary.

1. Review the Day 1 scope, prerequisite from Day 0, and supervisor instructions before touching software, accounts, cables, power, rigging, networks, or equipment.
2. Confirm the authorized lab/equipment boundary, owner, asset IDs, workspace condition, backup/rollback state, emergency procedure, and any PPE or spotter requirement.
3. Verify only the approved tools for today: Beyond LED screens, projectors, PPE, approved lifts/stands, distribution tools, checklists. Record versions, firmware, serial/asset references, calibration status, or configuration as relevant. Avoid unnecessary installation or updates.
4. Create Day_001_electrical_lifting_and_screen_safety with evidence, diagrams or src, checklists or tests, output, and report folders.
5. Capture a privacy-reviewed baseline photograph/screenshot and record expected result, measurement units, acceptance limit, and stop condition.
6. Complete the practical objective: Complete a supervised electrical, lifting, stand/rigging, cable-trip, power-down, and exclusion-zone readiness check before installing or energizing screens and video equipment.
7. Introduce or analyze only an approved controlled fault/edge case. Troubleshoot systematically, preserve evidence, and return the lab/equipment to its approved state.
8. Verify independently through a second instrument/path/test, clean rerun, configuration comparison, peer check, or supervisor sign-off. Distinguish evidence from proof.
9. Complete the discipline safety/ethics checklist, inventory/custody or cleanup check, and a professional report with honest limitations and assistance disclosure.

## 5. SAFETY, ETHICS, AND BEYOND LAB RULES

- Use approved lifts, stands, rigging, PPE, and spotters. Calculate power, secure equipment and cables, establish exclusion zones, and follow approved power-down rules before connector or module work.
- Use only assigned labs, equipment, data, accounts, frequencies, networks, repositories, venues, and test targets. Stop if authorization or ownership is unclear.
- Do not expose secrets, private/client data, personal communications, production identifiers, unsafe images, or unrelated backgrounds in code, prompts, repositories, recordings, photographs, screenshots, or reports.
- Never bypass guards, interlocks, PPE, access controls, rated loads, electrical protection, change approval, licences, or vendor limits. Do not improvise unsafe adapters, rigging, mains power, scans, exploits, or public exposure.
- Use approved rollback, mute/power-down, backup, snapshot, restore, isolation, or safe-strike procedures before and after changes. Report accidental exposure, injury risk, damage, data loss, or boundary crossing immediately.
- Disclose AI/tool assistance and verify every generated instruction, calculation, configuration, claim, measurement, and recommendation. Record time, errors, troubleshooting, incidents, limitations, and equipment condition honestly.

## 6. SELF-CHECK QUESTIONS

1. Can you explain Electrical, Lifting, and Screen Safety to a supervisor in under two minutes without reading?
2. What evidence proves that you completed “Complete a supervised electrical, lifting, stand/rigging, cable-trip, power-down, and exclusion-zone readiness check before installing or energizing screens and video equipment.” rather than merely watching or copying a result?
3. Which safety, privacy, security, electrical, mechanical, hearing, data-quality, operational, or authorization failure is most relevant today?
4. What measurement or acceptance criterion did you use, and what are its limitations?
5. How did you independently verify the result and restore the approved state?
6. What would you check first if the demonstration failed five minutes before review?
7. Why is the result ready—or not ready—for real use, and who must approve the next action?

## 7. EVIDENCE CHECKLIST

- Collect evidence while working—not only at the end.
- Use clear filenames and remove secrets, personal/client information, notifications, and unrelated content.
- **day-001_electrical-lifting-and-screen-safety_baseline.png** — Privacy-reviewed baseline showing the authorized workspace, isolation/boundary, assigned tools or equipment, and safe starting state.
- **day-001_electrical-lifting-and-screen-safety_practical.zip** — Configurations, code, diagrams, checklists, measurements, tests, and outputs needed to reproduce the work; exclude secrets and unauthorized data.
- **day-001_electrical-lifting-and-screen-safety_verification.txt** — Expected versus observed result, acceptance criterion, and independent second test, measurement, peer review, or supervisor sign-off.
- **day-001_electrical-lifting-and-screen-safety_safety-restoration.txt** — Completed safety/ethics check plus proof of rollback, cleanup, inventory/custody, safe power-down/strike, or restored lab state as applicable.
- **day-001_electrical-lifting-and-screen-safety_report.pdf** — Professional report covering scope, concepts, tools/equipment, procedure, measurements, results, risks, verification, troubleshooting, limitations, restoration, assistance disclosure, and references.

**Required submission:** Baseline evidence, completed practical artifact, independent verification, safety/restoration record, and short professional report.

**Pass tip:** Supervisors assess correct technique, measurable evidence, safety, honest troubleshooting, verified restoration, and professional documentation—not a perfect first attempt.

**Required report sections:** Title and metadata; Objective, scope, authorization, and boundary; Concepts in the student’s own words; Environment, equipment, software, versions, and asset references; Inputs, diagrams, and baseline state; Procedure and change record; Measurements, results, and acceptance criteria; Independent verification; Safety, ethics, security, privacy, quality, and human approval; Troubleshooting and rollback; Cleanup, restoration, custody, and residual risk; Limitations and next step; AI/tool assistance disclosure; Official/vendor references.
